findings.title: Call to a nonexistent no-argument passkeys helper prevents compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only inherited method introduced in `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. Neither `UsernameForm` nor `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` supplies a no-argument overload. This source therefore does not compile; pass `context.getUser()` or add the intended overload.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are no longer initialized for an anonymous initial login
findings.body: The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` predicate requires a non-null user. On the initial username/password page `context.getUser()` is normally null, so `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped even when passkeys are enabled for the realm. As a result the form does not receive the conditional-UI flag, challenge, RP ID, or WebAuthn attributes, disabling passkey/conditional-UI login before a user has been selected. The previous code intentionally initialized WebAuthn in this null-user branch; retain that behavior while also initializing it for reauthentication.

findings.title: Initial-login error responses drop conditional-passkey form state
findings.body: The error challenge now calls `fillContextForm` only when `context.getUser()` is non-null. For an anonymous initial login (for example an invalid username/password submission), the returned form is missing the conditional-passkey attributes and a fresh challenge despite passkeys being enabled. This regresses retry behavior by making the passkey UI disappear after an initial-login validation error; the condition should allow enabled passkeys when no user is selected as well.
